paper_title: Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse
caption: Predicting narrative frames using oracle (human-annotated) and noisy (predicted) labels for their , , , and ; the results are macro-averaged F1.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the macro-averaged F1 scores for predicting narrative frames using three different prompting strategies—“Basic prompt,” “Structured prompt + oracle,” and “Structured prompt + predicted”—across three language models: Gemini, GPT-4o, and Sonnet. The vertical axis represents the F1 score, ranging from 0 to 0.7 in increments of 0.1. For each model, three bars are grouped side by side: the blue bar for “Basic prompt,” the orange bar for “Structured prompt + oracle,” and the green bar for “Structured prompt + predicted.” Across all models, the “Structured prompt + oracle” condition consistently achieves the highest F1 scores—approximately 0.60 for Gemini, 0.58 for GPT-4o, and 0.52 for Sonnet. The “Structured prompt + predicted” condition yields intermediate performance, with scores around 0.35 for Gemini, 0.47 for GPT-4o, and 0.42 for Sonnet. The “Basic prompt” condition performs the lowest in all cases, with scores near 0.32 for Gemini, 0.26 for GPT-4o, and 0.34 for Sonnet. The chart visually emphasizes the performance gap between oracle-supervised and predicted-label conditions, as well as the consistent improvement over basic prompting, with GPT-4o showing the largest gain from structured prompting with oracle labels.
